setup: Pulley about collarbone height when standing
Bar or rope; a close neutral grip suits most
Kneel or stand a step back, facing the cable
execution: Sweep the handle down in an arc to your thighs
Lift your chest just enough to clear the cable
Lean forward slowly into the stretch
faults: Don't bend your elbows into a pushdown
Don't yank out of the stretched position
Don't sit far back and turn it into a crunch
Don't let the stack pull your arms up fast

notes: Reverse slowly at the stretched, arms-overhead position: the shoulder is at the end of its range there.
If the shoulder is uncomfortable at the top, try another grip width or handle, or stop the stretch a little short.
Kneel on a mat and keep the cable clear of your face as the handle passes it.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Straight-arm pulldown
regressions.reason: Standing with a fixed torso; a shorter range that is easier to control.

progressions.name: Lat prayer with a pause in the stretch
progressions.reason: A short hold at the top, arms overhead, adds time under tension without more load.

substitutions.name: Straight-arm pulldown
substitutions.reason: Same straight-arm lat pull, standing at a high pulley. Stack numbers aren't comparable.

substitutions.name: Dumbbell pullover
substitutions.reason: Similar straight-arm arc lying on a bench; load is one dumbbell.

substitutions.name: Lat pulldown
substitutions.reason: Vertical pull for the lats with the elbows bending; more weight and more biceps.

substitutions.name: Single-arm pulldown
substitutions.reason: One arm at a time on the cable; good when one side lags.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at chest height of a kneeling figure facing the cable column, pulley at about standing collarbone height on the far left. The cable line from the pulley to the hands must stay visible so the arc reads clearly.

keyPositions.label: Stretch
keyPositions.describe: Kneeling about a step back from the column, hips hinged so the torso leans well forward. Arms reach up and forward toward the pulley, elbows almost straight, lats stretched.

keyPositions.label: Halfway
keyPositions.describe: Handle sweeping down past the face in an arc, elbows still nearly straight. Chest lifting a little so the cable clears the head.

keyPositions.label: Finish
keyPositions.describe: Handle at or just past the thighs, arms by the body, elbows still nearly straight. Torso more upright than at the start.

ikHints: Knees and shins fixed on the floor
Hands fixed to the handle; cable runs straight from the pulley to the hands
Elbow angle stays nearly constant through the rep
guideBrief.barPath: An arc from in front of and above the head down to the thighs
emphasise: Arms stay nearly straight; the shoulders do the work
Torso leans forward into the stretch and lifts to finish
Slow turn at the stretched position

uncertain.note: Own entry rather than an alias of cable-straight-arm-pulldown: the lat prayer uses a lower pulley, a moving torso and usually a kneeling stance, so its stack numbers are higher and not comparable with the standing straight-arm pulldown. Ben may prefer to merge them.
The Human Kinetics description is standing; kneeling is a common variant for heavier loads (Henselmans, seen through a search summary only). Whether Ben kneels or stands is not known.
